items.title: NEW GPT 5.2: A Total Bloodbath
items.summary:
Brand new GPT-5.2 was released just hours ago and I tested it not on standard known benchmarks, but on my personal logic test for causal reasoning. 

This test is my base test for a lot of other LLMs, from Gemini 3 Pro to the latest OPUS. 
You find all my other test here in this playlist
https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLgy71-0-2-F0Rla8lu5ZldpYQUfXM_5bT

AT first impression, it seems to me, that the graph engine of 5.2 is blocking the complete solution path, if encountering a problem. 5.2 defines problems as pure roadblocks. THis would indicate that 5.2 move from a pure probability distribution (next token prediction)  to a restricted path on a graph. And there it encounters the roadblock, since now it is working on lower manifold. Interesting ... 

5.2 keeps the focus on this single graph traversal, unable to break free and find another path.  Can you write an instruction set to improve 5.2? Leave a comment. 

#gpt5_2
#aitesting 
#airesearch 
#openai 
#chatgpt 
#gpt5

items.title: How to Build AI Agents Capable of Competing in Real-World Settings
items.summary:
How can we create AI agents that achieve results comparable to human experts? AI agents developed by Sakana AI, such as “AI Scientist” and “ALE-Agent,” generate creative papers and algorithms. When evaluated under the same conditions as humans, they receive objective assessments that place them on par with specialists. This presentation will explain the technologies underpinning these cutting-edge AI agents, including scaling during inference.

--

人間のエキスパートに比肩するような成果を上げるAIエージェントは一体どのようにして作り出すことが出来るのでしょうか？Sakana AIが作成した「AI Scientist」や「ALE-Agent」といったAIエージェントは、創造的な論文やアルゴリズムを生み出し、人間と同じ条件での比較において、専門家に伍する客観的な評価を受けています。本講演ではこういった最先端のAIエージェントを支える推論時スケーリング等の技術について解説します。

items.title: Why Amazon Prioritizes Efficiency Over Explainability
items.summary:
In episode 947 of the SuperDataScience podcast, Jeffrey Li breaks down the two main types of forecasting problems: operational and strategic. He uses Amazon as an example of operational forecasting where accuracy and efficiency are prioritized over explainability for logistics. Conversely, he explains that strategic forecasting, such as Financial Planning and Analysis (FP&A), requires high interpretability to drive business decisions.

Additional materials: https://www.superdatascience.com/947

items.title: The arrival of AGI | Shane Legg (co-founder of DeepMind)
items.summary:
Shane Legg, Chief AGI Scientist and co-founder of Google DeepMind, has been talking about artificial general intelligence, or AGI, for more than a decade. So what’s changed? According to Shane, now is the time to take it seriously.

In this episode, Shane walks host Hannah Fry through his AGI framework, breaking down the levels from minimal AGI to full AGI, and his timelines for each. They discuss the economic and societal shifts AGI will bring, the potential impact on work, and the extraordinary possibilities for human flourishing.

items.title: Fully Connected Tokyo 2025: Opening Keynote with W&B Cofounders Lukas Biewald & Chris Van Pelt
items.summary:
This keynote reflects on the rapid acceleration of AI in 2025, as models scale exponentially and real-world adoption spreads across healthcare, law, development, and the enterprise. With benchmarks becoming saturated and agent workflows emerging, AI is fundamentally reshaping how software is built and used. The talk also highlights new challenges in reliability and production, and introduces how Weights & Biases and CoreWeave are enabling the next generation of model development and deployment at scale.

-- 

本講演では、AIが指数的に進化し、医療や法律、ソフトウェア開発など幅広い領域で実用化が急速に進む2025年の現状を概観します。生成AIや動画・音楽の品質向上、エージェントの普及により、企業の業務と市場に大きな変革が起きています。一方で、AI特有の非決定性により開発と運用には新たな課題も生じています。Weights & BiasesはCoreWeaveとの協業のもと、大規模モデル開発やエージェント運用を支える次世代のAI開発基盤を提供していきます。

items.title: Are We Building Superintelligence Backwards?
items.summary: Sara Saab, VP of Product at Prolific, challenges our assumptions about AI alignment by comparing it to human moral development. Just as we don't expect humans to be born with perfect predetermined morality, why should we expect it from AI? She explores building backwards from AGI and the emerging ecosystem of human-machine oversight.

items.title: Stop Overthinking Your Tech Stack
items.summary:
Stuck choosing a tech stack for your next AI project? You might be overthinking it.

My friend Shaw Talebi is an AI engineer who ships a lot of small AI SaaS projects fast. His rule is simple: build with what you already know. For him, that means Python for basically everything, OpenAI’s API by default, and using models like ChatGPT and Claude up front just to clarify the idea and pick what to implement first.

The goal at this stage is not the most scalable or beautiful system. It is to get from 0 to 1 quickly, validate in the real world, then iterate. That is why he keeps his stack simple, modular, and composable so he can reuse pieces across projects and scale the ones that work instead of throwing away a messy proof of concept.

So if you are stuck comparing frameworks and tools, that is your sign to stop Googling and start shipping with the tools you already know best. The stack matters less than your speed to feedback.

I’m Louis-François, PhD dropout, now CTO & co-founder at Towards AI. Follow me for tomorrow’s no-BS AI roundup 🚀

#ai #buildinpublic #python
